answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover checkpoint committed as checkpoint:ddb979d5-3701-3e98-774d-efa6f020ac8d. The import remains a verified, retained audit package; no second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

claims.value: The completed import `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z` preserves the original 21,674,717-byte `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3` and a verified extracted tree under Git-ignored `raw/`. The ZIP contains 123 entries including directories and 115 manifested files plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`; `unzip -t` and every packaged SHA-256 passed. `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` remain tracked for auditability, while the raw duplicate third-party corpus, personalized save context, generated binaries, and legacy SQLite database remain retained but untracked.

The archive’s numeric data must not be labeled Steam build `23761620`: its source-site version and numeric game-build identity were not recorded reliably. The correct two-axis boundary is (1) source/game data: Update 1 internal version `35118973`, dated `2026-04-09`, contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`, with canonical SRDB `2.3.4` snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z` captured `2026-07-11`; and (2) executable observation: Update 1 Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, was merely the latest public executable observed at capture. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against that canonical snapshot.

The archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset were semantically duplicated by the richer RuptureOps corpus and were not installed as a competing snapshot. Selective promotion was limited to `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`, six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`, explicit assumptions in `sources/consumable-effects.json`, nine player-specific site/geography assets, and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected the building-shaped response that had overwritten the `airlock` item and the literal `$undefined` Training Corporation index. Duplicate prompt statements remain lossless provenance but yield one canonical fact; quoted assistant recommendations are not player observations, questions are not answers, and accepted plans are not installed state. No second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is superseded audit history: the player explicitly rejected its buffer-heavy direction and requested restoration of the earlier plan. It must not become current guidance. The July 11 authority is `Player save - progression and next builds.md`, whose staged Flowworks plan is explicitly a proposal, not confirmed construction: its 10-machine starter has Titanium and Wolfram Excavators and Smelters, Titanium Rod v2, Wolfram Powder v2, Wolfram Plate v2, one Stabilizer, one Impeller, and one Turbine; Valve expansion adds a Titanium Smelter, Sheet v2, Beam, Housing, Nozzle, and two Valves, with a second v1 Titanium Excavator only for an Impure node; two Pumps follow for Pressure Tank, the second Stabilizer waits until Scanner/levels 11–12, and HRS v2 is built only if imported-HRS recovery fails in practice. Exact live Corporation state and whether Flowworks construction began remain unresolved, so historical plans must not be represented as completed save state. The active RuptureOps pipeline and database remain authoritative over the archived SQLite database, snapshot JSON, delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script retained under `raw/`.

answer.answer: Grand Basin is corrected to the basin beside Mythic Cry, while Flowworks remains a relationally registered proposal. The Goethite and Oil satellites are adopted plans, not confirmed installations. Screenshot registration and SRDB coordinates remain separate until a transform is verified.

claims.value: The older provisional Grand Basin match to the Red Lake/Redleaf basin was wrong. Grand Basin Reserve is the broad basin north of the active production corridor, immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry”; Mythic Cry is in the mountains immediately west. The Grand Basin marker denotes the basin area, not a future Core. Its northern/northwestern pad is broad and relatively flat, and the first campus should remain east of the POI/cliff boundary with a combat exclusion strip.

Flowworks is the selected site between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. Faraday is east/southeast of Flowworks and immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn.” Flowworks is a proposed footprint, not a placed Core, so its pin is relational rather than confirmed installed infrastructure.

North is up on the named map, but its dashed site axis and visually terrain-registered site pins express relational placement rather than surveyed rail geometry. SRDB coordinates identify markers in the SRDB coordinate space; they must not be combined with screenshot registration as though a verified transform exists. Flowworks is only a proposed relational footprint, Grand Basin’s marker denotes an area rather than a Core, Faraday is terrain-registered rather than directly labeled in its crop, and Sunstone Station and Brimstone Utility have known parent relationships but exact pins remain open.

The adopted first permanent Goethite satellite, after Engine access and Selenian 9, is the safer triple northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`: three Laser Drills merge into one Goethite-only Cargo link delivering 45 raw Ore/min to a 1,600-unit Storage Depot v2. It is preferred because the closer western field around `1252–1472,2950–3282` overlaps scanner/hostile envelopes. The adopted first Oil satellite, after Future Health 11, is west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin at approximately `1234,3760`: one Oil Extractor and one Crude-only Cargo pair deliver 10 Crude/min into one V2 buffer feeding one GB-A Refinery. A second pair and Refinery are reserved, not initially built, because one Refinery consumes the full source plus large Titanium and Calcium feeds; the marker around `1351,4473` is a separate site. These are adopted plans, not confirmed installed state, and their approximate coordinates are SRDB-marker precision rather than screenshot registration.

answer.answer: The inherited archive request resolves to one verified canonical reconciliation. Duplicate forks should reopen the single continuation checkpoint; no repository files or existing dirty work were modified during this run.

claims.value: The task topology comprises `019f4f6d-169c-70e2-8de4-81722b41eee9` (initial Update 1 research/bootstrap), `019f5263-8bae-7d10-b944-0fd4a543afb9` (clean bootstrap and ownership split), `019f52a5-72aa-7c11-853c-5de258361b42` (general import/reconciliation), `019f52fa-6195-7701-96a2-da6ec7ef7a08` (live exploration continuation), `019f52fa-6917-78a3-b1e5-7e631263b4a5` (logistics fork), `019f52fa-7180-7552-a3b1-09be4c3ee493` (exploration fork carrying the same inherited import request), and `019f531d-ba10-7d50-958e-4cffc089c334` (rupture-cycle product research/native build). Several forks inherited the exact same `Star Rupture Game Analysis.zip` request and therefore are duplicate replays, not independent imports or corroboration.

Replay identity is the verified source archive SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3` paired with import ID `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z`. The ledger records `imported_at` as `2026-07-11T19:54:52Z`, byte size `21674717`, `115` manifested files, and `integrity_status` `verified`. A fork seeing that identity must reuse the immutable source copies, manifest/checksum ledger, and existing promotion receipts rather than importing again.

The existing successful reconciliation is canonical. The package is an external research import, not a competing canonical source snapshot: its duplicated item, building, recipe, progression, export, map, loot, and official-news data were not installed again; only distinct evidence was promoted. Its legacy reports retain the July 8 capture boundary and must not be relabeled as snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z` until ported and rerun. Dirty-tree safety requires the duplicate forks to perform no checkout, stash, branch, overwrite, cleanup, re-import, or promotion; this coordination run made no repository mutation, preserving pre-existing and concurrently active work.

Exactly one continuation checkpoint was committed: `checkpoint:5885001d-0b19-9b03-27a8-d4f36c48223c` at `.straylight/checkpoints/5885001d-0b19-9b03-27a8-d4f36c48223c.md`. Forked continuations should reopen it and perform no import or promotion when the archive SHA-256 and import ID match. A genuinely different identity requires checking repository truth and the dirty worktree before proposing a new reconciliation; validation is required only after future artifact changes and must not be reported as run otherwise.
